A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 37-page research work on fully heterogeneous weakly-coupled MDPs. The main text, algorithms, experimental figures, equations, and Appendices A–I support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original simulations demonstrating performance as the number of arms increases and comparing the proposed policy with ERC. Results appear in Section 5, Figures 1–2, with details in Appendix B.

after.justification: v6 retains the original simulation results in Section 5 and Figures 1–2, together with the experimental details in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the LP-derived single-armed policies, ID reassignment, and real-time action selection are unchanged. The added sentence in Section 3 only clarifies the existing shorthand name “ID policy.”

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same randomly generated fully heterogeneous WCMDPs and the same ten-type, single-budget setting with state-independent costs for the ERC comparison (Section 5 and Appendix B.1).

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same ERC comparator from Xiong, Wang, and Li, reference [46]. Its definition in Appendix B.2 and the LP upper-bound reference in both figures are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same arm counts from 100 to 3200, ten states, four actions, instance-generation procedures, budget settings, 20,000 simulation steps, and optimality-ratio metric.

E4.justification: The arm-count scaling experiment and ERC comparison are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or additional case study is added or removed in the main text or appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report four replications per arm count and confidence intervals calculated by the batch-means method with batch size 4000. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 contain identical plotted results. Both versions report the ID policy's optimality ratio approaching one as arm count increases, slightly outperforming ERC in the illustrated instance, and performing comparably in others.

T1.justification: The definitions, Assumption 1, Theorem 1's O(1/sqrt(N)) optimality bound, Proposition 1, and proofs in Appendices C–I are unchanged. Equation (10) retains the same mixing-time definition despite page reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same first-asymptotic-optimality claim for fully heterogeneous average-reward WCMDPs and the same projection-based Lyapunov contribution. No core claim is strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: The explanations of ID persistence and reassignment, mixing-time qualifications and generalization, unoptimized parameter dependence, and interpretation of the ERC comparison are unchanged. The shorthand clarification adds no substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same instance-generation and ERC implementation details, code pointer, and statement that results can be reproduced within 24 hours on a standard PC, exemplified by a six-core Intel Core i7.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference [2] and the Hong et al. unichain/aperiodicity paper receive publication-metadata updates; references [26] and [27] exchange numbers. These are updates to existing works, not additions.

P1.justification: Section 3 adds one sentence explicitly allowing “ID policy” as shorthand for “ID policy with reassignment.” Bibliographic metadata, venue abbreviations, and citation numbering are updated, while the remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The added sentence causes limited reflow on page 8, and bibliography edits alter reference ordering and line wrapping. Figures 1–2 and Algorithms 1–2 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v6 adds a small shorthand clarification in Section 3 and refreshes reference metadata, while preserving the theoretical arguments, appendix proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information. These editorial conveniences leave the paper's overall quality essentially unchanged.
